entry.title: Castaway, 1986 - ★★★
entry.content:
an interesting though not always successful exploration of hetero gender politics when they are supposedly stripped of all the societal stuff that we think makes them untenable. it turns out that adam and eve in the garden of eden is actually a pretty toxic fantasy to try to bring to life.

for a movie with oliver reed as a horny middle aged weirdo and amanda donohoe as a young beauty who spends more than 2/3rds of the runtime naked, there's really nothing sexy about this film. the story is frustrating and deeply sad, and both reed and donohoe turn in astonishingly good work on what had to be a hellish shoot. (this was donohoe's second film ever!!)

entry.title: The System, 1964 - ★★★★
entry.content:
something like a proto-dirty dancing, this aching and bittersweet tale of sex, class, and rock 'n roll in a beachside tourist town stars oliver reed as an aloof working-class fuckboy—a "seaside don juan" as he puts it—who finally catches feelings and finds out that it sucks, actually.

he's quite good in the role, finally allowed to be a person instead of a werewolf or sociopath or a psychopath or a 17th-century scoundrel. he's also so beautiful i want to scratch my own eyes out. director michael winner and cinematographer nicolas roeg seem almost uninterested in the cast of gorgeous women littering the shots, so intent are they on capturing reed's eyes and mouth and chest (and ass, in one extra wide shot). winner cast reed 5 more times; 20 years after this, roeg tapped reed for his somewhat naughty island adventure, castaway.

wikipedia tells me that ken russell saw the system and cast reed in the debussy film—and in between the two films reed was jumped in a pub and had to get 63 stitches, resulting in the facial scars that he thought would end his career. ken russell knew better, of course.

entry.title: The Scarlet Blade, 1963 - ★★½
entry.content:
passable though not terribly interesting hammer historical swashbuckler. i had it on in the background while working and only really looked up when oliver reed came onscreen to do his 'hulking sullen boy in love but too gruff to not be an ass about it' thing. i like that thing. i'm developing a real integrated theory of reed as an ideal 60s/70s romance hero in the bodice ripper tradition. it may be too scandalous of a theory to appear on letterboxd though...

entry.title: Dante's Inferno, 1967 - ★★★½
entry.content:
as fun as it is to see ken russell going balls to the wall in the devils (especially now that the film has been restored and uncensored after 55 years), there's something equally enjoyable about watching russell work within the confines of the bbc to put over a true story of lusty, drug-addicted, and promiscuous painters, poets, and models.

oliver reed certainly did make the camera his slave, as russell once said; as the titular dante gabriel rossetti, he is by turns boyish, bombastic, peevish, haunted, pathetic, sexy, and mournful. a snake crawls over his open eye and he barely blinks. reed was 29 years old here and could conjure up sexual chemistry with anyone and anything.

it's actually difficult for me to watch this film in 2026 and not see it as an eerie vision of the career and personal struggles reed himself would go on to have in the decades to come, as his own addiction (to alcohol) and at-times brutal petulance circumscribed his ability to work.
